request: Our campus has a lost-and-found desk and we want a simple board for it. Anyone who finds something can report it with a short description of the item, where they found it and the date they found it. People should be able to see all the items on the board and look at one item. When the owner comes to collect an item, the desk marks it as claimed and writes down the owner's name. An item that has already been claimed cannot be claimed again. We also want to see only the items that are still waiting for their owners.
summary:
I've built the lost-and-found board in `app.py`. All 7 automated checks pass. The items are saved in a file called `lost_and_found.db` in the project folder.

**What the board can do:**
- **`POST /items`**: report a found item. Give a short description, where it was found and the date it was found (written like `2024-05-01`). New items start out as waiting for their owner. If any of the three is missing or blank, or the date isn't a real date, the report is rejected.
- **`GET /items`**: see every item on the board, claimed or not.
- **`GET /items/unclaimed`**: see only the items still waiting for their owners.
- **`GET /items/{id}`**: look at one item. If there's no item with that number, you get a "not found" message.
- **`POST /items/{id}/claim`**: the desk marks the item as claimed and records the owner's name, which can't be blank. If someone tries to claim an item that's already been claimed, it's refused and the first owner's name stays on record.

**The checks confirm that:**
- reporting an item works, and incomplete reports are refused
- the full list and single items show up correctly
- claiming works and saves the owner's name
- an item can't be claimed twice
- the "still waiting" list leaves out claimed items

Anyone who can reach the board can use every action, including marking an item as claimed. You didn't ask for desk-only access, so I didn't add it.
